articleTitle: Model-free fuzzy controller for time delay systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: This paper introduces a control approach that integrates intelligent proportional-integral control (iPID) with fuzzy logic, aiming to enhance the adaptability, performance, and robustness of complex dynamic systems. The iPI controller employs a model-free approach that exceeds the constraints of conventional PID controllers by incorporating online model estimation and accommodating nonlinear dynamics, allowing for real-time parameter modifications to handle uncertainties and fluctuations. Fuzzy logic augments this by adeptly managing vague and uncertain data, thereby strengthening the controller’s functionality. The controller is applied to a mixing tank with dominant and variable delays. The evaluation of results indicates moderate improvement amid frequent perturbations and varying conditions. Simulations confirm its effectiveness and underscore its potential for use in robotics, industrial automation, and other challenging settings.

articleTitle: Evaluating information security in academic management systems under the ISO/IEC 27001 standard
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: An Academic Management System (AMS) is a technological tool used to manage academic processes in educational institutions. AMS helps optimise resources through data management, but it has information security challenges. Due to the need to inspect security in an AMS, this study aims to identify and evaluate risks and improve controls for AMS security. Adhering to international standards like ISO/IEC 27001:2013 is important for addressing cyber threats. The case study focuses on the AMS of the Technical University of Manabi, focusing on confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information. The methodology involves analysing AMS information security components using surveys conducted with the institution’s data centre personnel to determine the current system status. The results show that there are 48 active controls and 33 inactive ones, meaning that the AMS is partially protected according to the standard. Additionally, risks associated with likelihood and impact are identified, along with recommendations to strengthen AMS security management.

articleTitle: Design of a backup system powered by renewable energy sources for the operation of a textile industry in Quito
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: This research proposes the design of an energy backup system using renewable energy sources to ensure the continuity of electrical service in a textile industry operating under a 24-hour work regime. Using various engineering methodologies such as energy load surveys and efficiency indicators, photovoltaic solar panels were selected as the optimal renewable energy source. The results show improved energy efficiency and economic benefits, with surplus energy being sold to the national grid, reducing production costs. This work contributes to the company’s sustainability and environmental goals.

articleTitle: Level control simulation and fault prediction system using machine learning
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: This work explores the use of Machine Learning techniques for advanced level control and fault prediction in a coupled tank system. The main objective is to design a predictive model capable of improving liquid level regulation and enabling early fault detection, addressing the limitations of conventional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers in dynamic industrial environments. Two Machine Learning techniques, such as Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Random Forest, were used for level control and fault prediction, respectively. The results showed that MLP models with four hidden layers significantly reduced prediction errors, while Random Forests provided superior fault prediction accuracy due to their robustness against overfitting. Compared to traditional methods, the proposed Machine Learning-based control system demonstrates enhanced adaptability, precision, and stability in scenarios with high variability and noise. In addition, the system’s fault prediction capabilities improve predictive maintenance and operational efficiency, which are crucial for industrial safety and reliability. These facts highlight the potential of Machine Learning techniques to transform process control by addressing complex challenges and enabling smarter, more reliable industrial systems.

articleTitle: Advancing stem pedagogy through gamified 3D - printed educational prototypes: a PODS-driven framework for bridging theory and practice
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: This paper introduces a framework integrating 3D-printed prototypes with the PODS methodology (Prediction, Observation, Discussion, and Synthesis) to enhance STEM education. A case study using a 3D-Printed Spring-Powered Car demonstrates its effectiveness in teaching kinematics and dynamics through hands-on, iterative activities that foster critical thinking and collaboration. The approach bridges theory and practice, leveraging 3D printing and gamification to improve student engagement, motivation, and knowledge retention. This methodology, in addition to being adaptable and scalable, demonstrates that combining technological tools with active learning methodologies for teaching generates significant improvements in STEM education, leading to a deeper understanding of knowledge by students.

articleTitle: K9-Buddy: platform for robotics education and competencies
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Most educational robots are prefabricated and do not allow modifications, which limits their use to teaching programming. Additionally, robotic kits are expensive, making them difficult to acquire. This document presents a low-cost, open-source quadruped robot as a platform for STEAM education and use in robotics competitions. K9-Buddy is characterized by its simplicity in terms of hardware and software, and its mechanical design inspired by canine aesthetics. Despite its simplicity, K9-Buddy participated in the Robomatrix Continental 2023 competition, where it won first place in the Robot Dance category, in which it had to perform complex and synchronized movements autonomously. K9-Buddy’s success as a competition robot, its low cost, easy construction, and modification demonstrate its potential as an educational tool for learning.

articleTitle: White balance adjustment in hyperspectral images through statistical analysis
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: In this study, we address white balance calibration in hyperspectral images using statistical techniques. We employed the Senop HSC-2 hyperspectral camera, capable of capturing high-resolution images (1024 × 1024 pixels) across up to 1,000 spectral bands within the 450 to 800 nm range. Each pixel has a 12-bit depth, resulting in a data cube size of approximately 41,943,040 bytes. Exposure times were adjusted between 10 ms and 25 ms to optimize data quality under varying lighting conditions. The camera has a white reference part next to the image area while taking pictures. This is for later adjustments. A spot of 35 × 35 pixels, which equals 1,225 data points per color band, was chosen for checking. The data were lined up one after the other, and complex math methods were used to find best fix values for each spectral band, with a goal to correct color mistakes and boost accuracy. The findings show that using these math techniques allows better white balance fixing in hyperspectral imaging. This leads to better data quality and helps in many scientific and industrial uses.

articleTitle: Backlog management: analyzing user-reported and technically identified incidences in medical equipment maintenance
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Accurate medical diagnosis is crucial for human well-being, and modern technology has provided healthcare personnel with essential tools for monitoring, diagnosing, and treating diseases. This study examined the critical role of effective first-level maintenance in ensuring the functionality of medical equipment, focusing on a case study of a company specializing in the sale and maintenance of medical devices in Ecuador. This study analyzed incident rates and contributing factors for EEG and EMG devices in clinical settings, reporting 36 and 42 incidents for EEG and EMG, respectively. Incidents were classified as related to accessories, equipment, software, or unspecified causes, with more 50% incidents for both types of devices not defined by operators, highlighting the need for better reporting practices. Inexperience of the operator was a key factor, with 50% incidents reported by individuals with less than a year of experience. The financial losses from equipment downtime were significant, averaging $448/day for EEG and $620.25/day for EMG. The primary causes of failures included accessory-related problems, incorrect settings, and user errors, which could be mitigated by improved operator training and robust preventive maintenance programs. These findings underscore the importance of improving operator competence and implementing proactive maintenance to ensure equipment reliability and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis of harmonic mitigation in a photovoltaic energy microgrid for supply to an electronic load
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Photovoltaic systems (PFS) are a key alternative for electricity generation, although they face power quality problems due to harmonic distortion generated by the inverters implemented in these systems. For this reason, this study addresses the mitigation of harmonics in a microgrid fed by a PFS that supplies an electronic load. The microgrid was modeled in real time at Innovación en Redes y Telecomunicaciones Cotopaxi using neural networks to predict harmonics based on hourly irradiance and temperature data. By comparing measurements from the MP-200 Apogee pyranometer with data from the NASA website two scenarios of the photovoltaic system were analyzed: first with and then without a tuned filter, later validating the resu lts with a network analyzer. The results show that the implementation of a double-tuned passive filter reduced the voltage THD from 10.87% to 1.55% and the current THD from 40.80% to 1.42%, complying with IEEE 519-2014 standard. Furthermore, the NARX neural network achieved 95% accuracy in harmonic prediction, demonstrating the effectiveness of the approach in improving microgrid power quality and stability.

articleTitle: Systematic review of a voice-to-Ecuadorian sign language translator
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: In Ecuador, deaf people are facing several communication barriers due to the lack of tools for sign language translation. This study aims to make a systematic review of the current state of the field in Ecuador, analyzing how technologies have been applied to other translators in other countries, to have an approach of what is missing in Ecuador. Using the PRISMA methodology, searches were conducted in IEEE Xplore and Scielo. These findings highlight the use of artificial intelligence in these translators, also including 3D models, where most of this research is focused on India and the United States. Valuable information for the future development of a sign language translator for Ecuador.

articleTitle: Transformer framework for the fault detection of a reciprocating compressor
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Reciprocating compressors are crucial in the industrial sector, playing a key role in energy, manufacturing, and chemical engineering production processes. Effective health monitoring technologies can prevent failure risks, reduce unplanned downtime, and ensure production continuity. Although machine fault diagnosis technologies have developed rapidly, they still need improving with data collection, insufficient feature extraction, and weak generalization ability in practical applications. Traditional fault detection methods make it challenging to train models, especially when only healthy data and no faulty data are available. This study compares three unsupervised fault detection methods: autoencoders (AE), contrast abnormality detection (C-AD), and contrast one-class abnormality detection (COCA), focusing on which model is more compatible with the Transformer framework. The experimental results show that AE combined with the Transformer framework is more suitable for fault detection.

articleTitle: Dynamic VBR model of single-phase induction machines using ATPDraw
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: This work focuses on the dynamic modeling of the unbalanced single-phase induction machine, using the VBR (Voltage Behind Reactance) model, and considering its behavior under transient and steady-state conditions, developing the analysis in space vectors. The model was developed using the ATP-EMTP program and its graphical environment ATPDraw, and compared with models in MATLAB within the Simulink environment, employing circuits, TACS control modules, and the MODELS language. The simulation results include variables such as electrical torque, angular speed, winding currents, and flux linkages, with the aim of analyzing and validating the obtained results.

articleTitle: Achachay App: a community-driven innovation for flood data collection in urban and rural areas
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Floods are among the most frequent and devastating natural disasters, significantly impacting urban and rural communities worldwide. Achachay App is a mobile application designed to enhance flood data collection and analysis through direct community engagement. The app enables users to report real-time flood events by sharing detailed descriptions, geographic coordinates, and multimedia evidence such as photos or videos. Researchers use these community-sourced data to analyze and reconstruct watercourse behaviors that lead to flooding. Ecuador was selected for implementation as a pilot initiative, where the app successfully mapped flood-prone areas and secondary flows. These features aim to deepen understanding of the interplay between geological and climatic phenomena, supporting disaster preparedness and prevention. By bridging technology and community collaboration, theAchachay Appoffers valuable insights for policymakers to design sustainable public policies that mitigate risks and promote social and economic development in Ecuador.

articleTitle: SMART-MANAGER: a multi-user, multi-tenant informatics platform for remote management of internet network terminal devices based on the TR-069 protocol
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: The Rapid expansion of Internet networks requires robust and scalable solutions for remote management of Customer Premises Equipment (CPE), especially for small and medium-sized Internet service providers. This paper presents the SMART-MANAGER IT platform, a multitenant, multi-user system designed to address the complexities of centralized CPE management using the TR-069 protocol. The platform integrates the open source GenieACS server with a middleware layer that enhances interoperability through the Semantic Sensor Network (SSN) ontology. Key features include real-time device monitoring, efficient data processing, advanced security mechanisms (JWT and RBAC), and customisable dashboards tailored to different user roles. In a production environment, the system demonstrated remarkable scalability and performance, successfully managing 5,000 devices with minimal latency (average 25 ms) and maintaining stability under high load. The proposed architecture significantly reduces operational costs for small ISPs while ensuring seamless CPE management. This makes it a practical and scalable solution for large-scale IoT ecosystems. Future work will focus on integrating the TR-369 protocol to support next-generation device management and further enhance system capabilities.

articleTitle: Gear fault severity classification using acoustic emission peaks and Poincaré plots
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Acoustic Emission (AE) signals are broadband signals used for fault detection in rotating machinery. Acquiring AE signals requires high sampling frequencies, often exceeding 1 MHz, which necessitates significant memory resources for storage. This limitation renders such signals impractical for fault condition monitoring in applications where remaining useful life prediction is crucial. This research proposes a novel peak-based signal representation for AE signals. This representation significantly reduces the memory space required for storage. Furthermore, we propose a feature set derived from this representation, combining Poincaré plot-based and statistical features. We evaluate its effectiveness for classifying broken tooth fault severity in a spur gearbox. Using Random Forest models, we achieve the highest classification accuracy of 94.46%.

articleTitle: Towards the early detection of speech disorders in children applying manifold learning techniques: preliminary results
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Speech disorders in children can significantly hinder their social interaction, academic performance, and overall development. Early detection is crucial for effective intervention, yet current diagnostic methods often overlook the potential of video-based analysis. This study explores the application of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Autoencoder (AE) techniques to analyse video data, focussing on facial movements during speech to facilitate the clustering of children with distinctive speech features. Using a database of 60 video recordings, embeddings were generated and evaluated on the basis of their ability to reconstruct the original data, the results visualised through t-SNE. PCA demonstrated superior performance with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0023 for 78 dimensions, while AE achieved its lowest MSE of 0.0093 with 15 dimensions. In particular, embeddings with lower MSE showed better clustering tendencies. This study highlights the potential of integrating video-based analysis into machine learning frameworks to improve the accuracy and depth of speech disorder diagnostics.

articleTitle: Gigabit American advanced networks: emulation of the 2024 backbone topology under IPv6
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Time in time, Internet Service Providers around the world make updates in backbone topology and infrastructure, it includes de commercial Internet and the Internet 2, also known as advanced networks or national research and education networks. Previous works offered the connectivity and management emulation of the backbone network for CANARIE, INTERNET2 and CLARA, the three advanced networks in America for Canada, USA and Latin American under IPv4 for the 2019 topology. In this the work some updates are offered, this way it is considered the connectivity and management emulation for the four backbone networks under IPv6 for the updated topology up to 2024 and updates for BGP-4 for Autonomous Systems in 2024, also is indicated the use of virtual machines and IReasoning MIB Browser software for the network management. When integrating the three topologies, the backbone network resulting covers 13 countries in the continent. The resulting emulations review the management assessment and topology show how some topologies are evolving in case of CANARIE and INTERNET2, but CLARA is having some difficult to maintain the same countries connected, some of the decisions are taken based on the use and development of strategic projects. These results could be useful for next upgrades and the grow of the advanced networks in the continent.

articleTitle: Reverse engineering analysis applied to the upgrade of a WAN in a medical supplies company
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Nowadays, having an updated wide area network in their topology, technological equipment and information security is a must to be competitive in any industry or commerce. Forward engineering is very common for new design or developments for new business, however on many occasions companies grow in a disordered way until they reach good surpluses and continue growing. Then there is a point in the development of the company when looking for competitiveness to be a respect to other competitors implies making improvements. In this work the reverse engineering was applied to a WAN in a medical supplies company, with offices in five buildings located in four states in Mexico, where it was required because no information and registers were available about the way it works and how to make the upgrade. A full assessment was developed, vulnerabilities and weaknesses were found then corrections and a proposal for the upgrade was done.

articleTitle: Proposed architecture for a patient management and classification system in the triage process
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Managing patients efficiently has become increasingly challenging due to the rising number of cases with complex diseases and complications. An effective triage system is essential, requiring speed and accuracy, as global healthcare systems face mounting pressures from urbanization and emerging health issues. Despite advancements in technology, triage remains a labor-intensive process, as sorting patients promptly and diagnosing conditions efficiently are still difficult and costly tasks. Moreover, while comprehensive patient information is critical, collecting extensive data without clear purpose remains impractical. This paper reviews various solutions developed to address the challenges of triage using Artificial Intelligence techniques. It examines the main features of these solutions, their strengths and weaknesses, and the existing gaps to propose an architecture for a new AI model that streamlines the triage process.

articleTitle: Building management system control for home automation with HDL Buspro
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: This paper talks about a control thing for buildings, called Building Management System (BMS). It looks at handling the HDL Buspro communication stuff. The main goal of this system is to help collect and look at a lot of energy usage data using software that’s free and open-source. To connect BMS with devices, they use User Datagram Protocol (UDP). This protocol works on the transport part, letting messages move around without needing to set up a connection first between sender and receiver. So, UDP helps send data without waiting for each other, making things faster and easier. The suggested BMS is flexible and easy to use, which makes it good for different building management tasks. Using this system can lead to better efficiency in operations, more productivity, and happier users. Plus, it helps save energy by managing resources better in automated places where it’s used.

articleTitle: Storytelling and stem: a scoping review
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Storytelling is a powerful pedagogical tool that enhances critical thinking, creativity, and student engagement by presenting complex concepts through narratives. This scoping review examines the integration of storytelling in Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education, focusing on its implementation, methodologies, and outcomes across primary and secondary levels. A total of 61 studies were analyzed to map key aspects of the interventions, including participant characteristics, educational levels, research approaches, and tools utilized. Results indicate a predominance of storytelling interventions in primary levels and science-related subjects, often employing digital narratives. The findings highlight the potential of storytelling to develop technical, cognitive, and socio-emotional skills, such as critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration, fostering interest in STEM fields. However, gaps persist in terms of the inclusion of storytelling strategies designed and applied to minority groups such as women and indigenous populations. This review underscores the need for more diverse, inclusive and rigorous approaches to maximize the impact of storytelling in STEM education.

articleTitle: Neural networks in disinformation detection in Spanish: a comparative analysis between BERT and BETO
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Fake news detection has become a critical challenge in the digital age, particularly in Spanish-speaking environments where research remains limited. This study compares the performance of two transformer-based natural language processing models: BERT and BETO. While BERT is a multilingual model trained on vast datasets from multiple languages, BETO is exclusively pretrained on Spanish, enabling it to capture the unique nuances and context of the language with greater accuracy. Using a balanced dataset of Spanish news articles, both models were trained and evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results reveal that BETO significantly outperforms BERT, achieving an accuracy of 90.95% compared to 45.73%. These findings highlight the importance of linguistic specialization for effective misinformation detection and suggest that expanding data corpora and exploring hybrid approaches—integrating multilingual and language-specific models—could further enhance performance in diverse contexts.

articleTitle: A review on relevant failure modes in electric machines
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Rotating electrical machines play an important role in industrial and power generation systems, yet their reliability is challenged by diverse failure modes due to mechanical, electrical, and environmental factors. This paper presents a review of common failure modes in synchronous and asynchronous machines, with a focus on prevalent faults such as bearing wear, winding degradation, rotor bar fractures, and permanent magnet demagnetization. The analysis examines the root causes, cascading effects, and interdependencies of these failures, revealing that bearing failures constitute 51% of total faults, while stator and rotor failures represent 16% and 5% respectively. A Failure Mode and Effects Analysis identifies critical components and guides the development of maintenance strategies. This study contributes to the advancement of fault diagnosis and prevention, enhancing operational reliability in rotating electrical machinery, while providing a foundation for developing intelligent maintenance systems.

articleTitle: Detection and adaptation to concept evolution in data streams: an integral framework
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: In the era of big data, machine learning systems face the challenge of adapting to dynamic environments, where data patterns change unpredictably, known as concept drift. In addition, new data classes may emerge, a phenomenon known as concept evolution, which represents a growing challenge in many real-world applications. Most current approaches focus on changes in data but lack efficient mechanisms to handle new classes. An additional problem is the availability of labeled data, as many algorithms assume that labels will be continuously available, which is unrealistic. Furthermore, many methods rely on user-defined parameters, which can affect performance. This paper proposes an integrated framework that combines data mining techniques to handle both concept drift and concept evolution in data streams, efficiently adjusting models to maintain performance in non-stationary environments. Results on two real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: AI-based predictive and detection models for Avian Pox caused by Avipoxvirus Spp in the Galápagos Islands
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Predicting infection byAvipoxvirus spp, the causative agent of avian pox, in endemic Galápagos Islands species such as theGeospiza fuliginosafinches, represents an innovative approach to controlling viral diseases in vulnerable ecosystems. This study uses artificial intelligence-based predictive models trained on a database compiled from previous research. The database was balanced and subjected to data augmentation like synthetic minority oversampling and tablediffusion. Compared with alternative studies, where the data is converted from tabular data into an image achieving a recall of 85%; our results achieve a recall of near 100% using a multi-state analysis over susceptible-infectious-recovered models in infectious diseases for populations of the European serins (Serinus serinus), highlighting the anticipatory capacity for early identification of outbreaks and risk factors. This predictive tool not only strengthens biodiversity protection in the archipelago but also supports the development of targeted vaccines and treatments, ensuring the preservation of this unique ecosystem and providing a model applicable for monitoring other infectious diseases in bird populations.

articleTitle: Designing a high school computational thinking test using evidence-centered design
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: The development of computational thinking as a cognitive skill is crucial in the digital age. However, there remains no consensus on its definition or measurement. This study aims to address this gap by developing an instrument to estimate the level of computational thinking using an evidence-centered design approach. The proposed framework integrates cognitive theory, educational research, and psychometric modeling to create a comprehensive and reliable assessment tool. The instrument consists of two scenarios with a total of 59 items divided into six questions. It was validated by experts in the field, achieving a content validity index of 0.76. The test was administered to a sample of 100 students from three secondary schools in Lima, Peru, and analyzed using Bayesian confirmatory factor analysis and parametric tests. The results indicate that the model effectively assesses algorithmic thinking, critical thinking, and problem solving skills, regardless of prior programming experience. However, the assessment of creativity requires further refinement. This research contributes to evidence-based educational policy and practice in secondary education, offering a foundation for future improvements in the evaluation of computational thinking.

articleTitle: On the use of AI algorithms applied to strong motion records for the prediction of earthquake fault mechanisms
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Earthquake focal mechanisms are derived from moment tensor solutions and provide insights into earthquake rupture characteristics, including strike, dip, and rake angles. Common methods for analysing seismic records (seismograms) include first motion polarity of P-waves, waveform inversion, and amplitude analysis. However, these methods often require significant human intervention. With the increasing availability of strong-motion earthquake records (accelerograms) from diverse epicentral distances, depths, and tectonic regions, there is potential to analyse these records in non-traditional feature spaces—such as shape, texture, and pixel intensity—to predict earthquake fault mechanisms. Artificial intelligence (AI) advancements, especially machine learning algorithms, allow for the analysis of large datasets and the extraction of repeated patterns or behaviours, which could enhance earthquake characterization. While traditional approaches typically rely on time-domain analysis requiring extensive preprocessing, this study aims to develop a non-traditional workflow to classify strong ground motion signals based on their focal mechanism types using machine learning. The proposed workflow involves the following steps: (1) Transforming each signal from the time domain (1D) to the frequency domain via a spectrogram, creating a 2D image representation; (2) Segmenting the spectrogram image to extract shape features; (3) Generating texture-and pixel-intensity-based descriptors. The optimal feature subset is then fed into four machine learning classifiers—random forest, support vector machine, naive Bayes, and an artificial neural network. The method demonstrates efficient classification of seismic records, offering a pathway for automating the analysis and improving overall efficiency.

articleTitle: Automated segmentation and classification of meningiomas using AI techniques
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Accurate and early detection of the degree of malignancy of meningiomas is essential to optimize treatment and improve patient outcomes. However, traditional diagnostic methods often face challenges due to the variable locations and sizes of tumors, which complicate accurate identification and classification. In this study, we introduce a web application that integrates advanced artificial intelligence techniques for automated segmentation and classification of meningiomas on T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Our system employs a 3D U-Net convolutional neural network for precise tumor segmentation and tree-based machine learning models such as Extra Trees and Random Forest for tumor grade classification. These models achieved F1-scores of 94% and 92%, respectively, to differentiate grade I (benign) and grade II (atypical) meningiomas. A total of 112 radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics, which included sets of three-dimensional shape descriptors, gray-level co-occurrence matrix features, and first-order statistical metrics. The developed web application provides an accessible and user-friendly tool for medical professionals, enabling the uploading, processing, and automated analysis of MRI scans for the detection and classification of meningiomas. The results not only demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, but also offer a solid foundation for future research aimed at enhancing diagnostic accuracy and clinical management of meningiomas through methods based on artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Performance of digital skills from student to school teacher in Ecuador and Peru according to the adaptation of the Charlotte Danielson model
publicationTitle: International Conference on Technological Innovation and AI Research (ICTIAIR 2025)
abstract: Contemporary education faces significant challenges in the integration of digital competencies, essential for teacher training. This study assesses the performance in digital competencies of university students in teacher training from Ecuador and Peru, using the Charlotte Danielson Assessment Framework, adapted to a digital context. The general objective was to analyze and compare the dimensions of Planning and Preparation, Classroom Environment, Instruction, and Professional Responsibilities in both countries. The problem identified lies in the disparities in the technological preparation of future teachers, which impacts educational quality. To address this, a quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study was conducted with a sample of 876 students (438 per country). A validated questionnaire with a Cronbach's Alpha of 0.981 was used, distributed through Google Forms and adjusted through two pilot surveys. The data were analyzed with structural equation modeling (SEM) and principal component analysis (PCA). The main findings revealed that Ecuadorian students obtained higher average scores in all dimensions, although with greater variability. Furthermore, the PCA confirmed a unidimensional structure that explains 83.4% of the variance. The findings highlight the need to improve digital skills in Peru and ensure equity in Ecuador, promoting specific educational policies to strengthen teacher training in both countries.
